what_it_does: Training or running large AI models across many chips requires the chips to constantly exchange data (for example, sharing updated weights or passing partial results around a ring of chips). When you combine several splitting strategies at once — slicing the model by layers, by attention heads, and by data batch simultaneously — the system ends up sending some of the same information multiple times under different names, which wastes time and link capacity. Chimera analyzes the data-exchange steps for each splitting strategy, finds those duplicate messages, and merges them into a single combined message that carries all the necessary information in one trip. The result is fewer blocking waits and higher compute utilization across the chip cluster.
